meaning: to stay positive and cheerful when things are difficult
example: Keep your chin up; the exam results will be better than you think.
origin: Thought to come from boxing, where lowering the chin leaves a fighter open to a punch

wrong_meanings.meaning: to lift your head to look at the sky
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This describes a physical action, not the emotional meaning of the idiom.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to become angry and shout at someone
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom describes staying calm and hopeful, not losing your temper.
The idiom has nothing to do with food or refusing meals.

explanation: 'Keep your chin up' is said to encourage someone to stay positive during a hard time. The physical picture of holding the head high suggests confidence.
